people.role: Mistress of Vũ Linh Đường since 1150: rain-bell warning arrays and bronze casting; keeps the warding bells on the walls of Thu Trì Thành
people.appearance: A neat, grey-eyed woman with burn scars on both wrists, who stops talking whenever a bell rings anywhere and resumes at the same word.
people.backstory: Ân Thanh Linh was born at the hall in 1010, eighty years after the founder Chung Thiết Liên (chung_thiet_lien) brought his lamp-casters south from Thanh Đăng Trấn and turned them to bells (V148, V149). The Tower had put out its lamps, so it would need to hear. At twenty she cast a bell for the Nhiếp family that rings only when someone is listening at a door. The Tower's spymaster still wears it. In 1062 she cast Thu Phần's grave bell. In 1105 she hung the hall's first bell line over the forest road (N-vu_linh-02). In 1150 the founder's son Chung Tàn Hưởng (chung_tan_huong) stepped down and gave her the hall, saying she heard bronze better than he did (N-vu_linh-03). She keeps the bells on the walls of Thu Trì and the lines along the forest roads, and she listens to all of them. For a century she has argued bronze by letter with the Tower's forge master Thạch Liên Hoàn (thach_lien_hoan). He forges in lightning; she casts in a charcoal fire and hangs the bell in a living tree to teach it to listen. The Tower's envoy Hứa Thanh Diêm (hua_thanh_diem) visits her before any other vassal.
people.wants: That the bells on Thu Trì's walls never ring for a war in her lifetime; and the last word in her century of letters.
people.secret: Inside Thu Trì's walls she hung a second line of bells that no one knows of, tuned to the Hall of Echoes' own listeners. For fifty years she has known every ear the Tower keeps in the south, and she has written it all down.

people.role: Grand elder; the founder's son, head 1060-1150, who gave the hall to Ân Thanh Linh
people.appearance: A huge, slow old caster with one ear gone to a cracked pour, who keeps an unlit blue lamp on his tea table.
people.backstory: Born at Thanh Đăng Trấn, the town of the blue lamps, in the year the Night Rain Edict put the Tower's lamps out (C167). He walked south at twenty-five behind his father Chung Thiết Liên (chung_thiet_lien) and learned to cast bells instead. He led the hall for ninety years after his father died at the pour, and in 1150 he gave it to Ân Thanh Linh (an_thanh_linh), who could hear what he could not. He has not lit his father's last lamp since 905.

people.role: Keeper of the warding bells on the walls of Thu Trì Thành
people.appearance: A tidy man in a grey coat with a ring of small keys at his belt, one for each bell tower on the wall.
people.backstory: A Thu Trì chandler's son who has walked the city walls every night for sixty years, oiling the bells and listening. He drinks with the Tower's ear at the ferry inn, Lục Nhĩ Thính (luc_nhi_thinh), and each knows what the other is. He does not know about the second line of bells inside the walls, and Ân Thanh Linh (an_thanh_linh) has not told him.

people.role: Mistress of the furnace: the hall's master caster at the pour
people.appearance: Broad and red-armed, with her hair burned short and a leather apron black with bronze.
people.backstory: The founder's great-granddaughter, raised at the furnace. Every bell the hall has cast in fifty years has been poured by her hands, and she resents that the casting is called Ân Thanh Linh's (an_thanh_linh). She writes the technical half of the letters to the Tower's forge, and Thạch Liên Hoàn (thach_lien_hoan) is the only man alive she thinks pours as well as she does.

people.role: The mistress's true disciple, who has tried nine times to cast a listening bell
people.appearance: A quick young woman with nine small cracked bells on a cord round her neck.
people.backstory: Born at the hall to two casters. Ân Thanh Linh (an_thanh_linh) took her as her true disciple at twenty-five, and she has spent fifteen years trying to cast a bell like the one the mistress made at twenty. Nine have cracked in the pour, and she wears them all. She suspects the mistress has not taught her the whole seal, and she is right.

people.role: Founder of Vũ Linh Đường (930): a lamp-and-chain caster of Thanh Đăng Trấn who turned to bells
people.backstory: A caster of Thanh Đăng Trấn who made the town's blue lamps and the Tower's bronze rain-chains. When the Night Rain Edict put the Tower's lamps out (C167, A274), the lamp trade died, and in 930 the lamp-makers went to Hạnh Hoa Thị (V148). Chung took his casters south above Thu Trì instead and turned them to bells (V149): if the Tower would not see at night, it would have to hear. He died at the pour in 1060, under a bell that cracked. His son Chung Tàn Hưởng (chung_tan_huong) kept the cracked bell, and in 1150 gave its bronze to Ân Thanh Linh (an_thanh_linh).
